text: I can bear this no longer—I must and will end it.” There was too much colour in her cheeks, too much energy in her manner, too much firmness in her voice. The little book of Hartright’s drawings—the fatal book that she will dream over whenever she is alone—was in one of her hands. I began by gently and firmly taking it from her, and putting it out of sight on a side-table. “Tell me quietly, my darling, what you wish to do,” I said. “Has Mr. Gilmore been advising you?” She shook her head.
